title: Stream Convergence: ergonomic async-iterator ↔ web-stream handoff for TS SDK
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: The TypeScript SDK currently exposes separate streaming primitives (AsyncIterator-based and WHATWG ReadableStream-based) that are awkward to use together. Teams building client integrations need a predictable, low-overhead way to hand a live generation stream between code that expects an AsyncIterator and code that expects a ReadableStream without copying buffers or losing cancellation/backpressure semantics.

Goal: Deliver a small, well-documented ergonomic bridge (library + examples) that lets application code seamlessly hand off, duplicate, or convert streams across the two runtime models while preserving: cancellation propagation, backpressure, error semantics, and streaming identity for telemetry and tracing. The work should be runtime-agnostic (Node/Deno/browser) and fit into our existing TS SDK surface with minimal footprint and clear migration path for customers.

Out of scope: building a new universal streaming runtime, rewriting existing SDK internals, or adding language-level features. This ticket focuses on an ergonomic shim and canonical examples and a small number of helpers in the SDK package.
acceptance_criteria: A tiny library (<= 120 LOC core) in the TS SDK that exposes two primary helpers: asyncIteratorToWebStream() and webStreamToAsyncIterator()
Cancellation in consumer code (abort signal or iterator.return()) is propagated to the underlying request and cleans up KV cache/transport sockets
Backpressure respected so that large-burst workloads do not cause unbounded memory growth in Node/browser environments
End-to-end example added to docs showing: a) passing a ReadableStream to a React Suspense consumer, b) consuming the same stream as for-await-of in a server-side job
Benchmarks demonstrating <10% median token-latency overhead for adapter path at 8 concurrent streams compared to native async iterator path
Type signatures that are idiomatic for TS consumers with clear JSDoc/TS examples and no any leaks
Landing PR with CI green, unit + integration tests for cancellation and error propagation, and a changelog entry
tech_notes: Design notes: prefer zero-copy transfer where possible; avoid dual-buffering by streaming underlying Uint8Array chunks directly and mapping to TextDecoder where necessary.
API prototypes: asyncIteratorToWebStream(asyncIter, {signal?, highWaterMark?}) -> ReadableStream; webStreamToAsyncIterator(stream, {signal?}) -> AsyncGenerator

Cancellation: wire iterator.return() to controller.close() + call underlying transport abort (via provided onCancel callback). When ReadableStream consumer cancels, call iterator.return() if present to allow graceful shutdown.

Backpressure strategy: use ReadableStream default queuing with configurable highWaterMark and a small internal buffer in the adapter. Avoid setImmediate loops; use microtask scheduling and explicit pull/read coordination.
Error propagation: map underlying transport errors to both stream error and iterator.throw(); keep stack/context to aid telemetry correlation IDs.

Runtime differences: Node ReadableStream vs browser ReadableStream subtle differences in queuing; feature-flag Node-specific small shim to unify the controller.wait behavior. Deno should follow browser shape.
Telemetry: attach a stable stream-id when creating adapters (uuid v4 or incremental) so Console traces can join AsyncIterator and WebStream traces as a single logical stream.
Performance expectations: primary path should be inlined and not allocate per-token closures. Use an iterator loop with single try/catch around read-pull logic to reduce allocations.
Testing plan: unit tests for conversion, simulated cancellation timeouts, fuzz test for high-churn small-chunk tokens, and a light benchmark harness in CI job that runs in Node 18/20 matrix.
decisions: Ship a shim in the SDK package (not a separate repo) to reduce friction for adoption
Expose two minimal helpers instead of a large utility surface to keep developer mental model simple
Prefer signal-based cancellation (AbortSignal) but also support iterator.return() to accommodate both idioms
No automatic duplication of streams (tee) in core helpers; provide a separate example showing how to tee when necessary
Do not change existing public streaming interfaces; keep helpers opt-in to avoid breaking customers

2026-03-12 - Reviewer (Sofia Martinez): Feedback on PR: ensure AbortSignal propagation, add test for iterator.return() driving transport.abort(), and add TypeScript types for onCancel callback. Also requested example for React and Node consumers.

2026-03-13 - Marco Nguyen: Addressed review comments. Changed internal scheduling to use a single pull loop which reduced synthetic overhead to ~6% median. Added telemetry stream-id header. Updated PR.

2026-03-14 - QA (Ravi Shah): Integration test flaky on Node 18 matrix when highWaterMark set to 0. Reproduced locally; suggested fallback to highWaterMark 1 for Node 18 until we detect native bug. Filed follow-up: ENG-100901.

2026-03-14 - Aisha Patel: Merging plan: land adapter helpers behind a minor feature flag for a week, monitor the streaming dashboard (https://dashboards.redwood.ai/streams/adapter-overview) for error rates and latency regressions before wide release.
